input.description: Find duplicate detection logic in controller

toolu_01SWaZUDxFU4XeYsk9eyH6UJ.description: Find duplicate detection logic in controller

content.text:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The change is well-placed in most respects: `IdentityKeyUtils` follows the existing `E164PhoneNumbers` static-utility convention in the `util` package, its javadoc correctly justifies why the helpers live outside the MapStruct mapper (matching the established note in `OwnerMapper.regionOf`), and `toIdentityKey` remains the single source of truth reused by both the DTO and the 409 check. But there is one concrete structural problem.

**Finding: `IdentityKeyUtils.sha256Hex` is a third copy of the SHA-256-to-hex routine.**

The new `sha256Hex` (lines 90–107 of `IdentityKeyUtils.java`) duplicates a digest-to-hex loop that already exists twice:

- `OwnerRestControllerV1.sha256UpperHex` (`OwnerRestControllerV1.java:350`) — identical `MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")` → `StringBuilder` → `String.format("%02X"/"%02x")` → `IllegalStateException("SHA-256 not available")` structure, differing only in hex case.
- `ClinicServiceImpl.householdIdFor` (`ClinicServiceImpl.java:302`) — the same loop, truncated to 12 chars.

The change introduces a dedicated hashing helper in the `util` package — which is exactly the natural home to consolidate these — yet leaves the two existing copies in place and adds a third. A maintainer would expect the new util to become the single hashing helper (e.g. a shared `sha256Hex` plus an upper-case/truncating variant, or a case parameter) with the controller and service delegating to it, rather than three near-identical private implementations of the same primitive spread across three layers.

Actionable: put the SHA-256 hex logic in one place (the new util) and have `OwnerRestControllerV1.sha256UpperHex` and `ClinicServiceImpl.householdIdFor` call through to it, so the digest-to-hex code exists once.

Minor (optional): in `findPossibleDuplicate`, `soundex(existing.getLastName())` is recomputed per existing owner even though `toIdentityKey(existing)` already computes the same soundex internally — the two soundex computations per candidate are inherent to hashing the key, but worth a note if a cheaper pre-filter is wanted later. Not blocking.
